findings.how_to_check: Tabulate the prevalence of ditto resolution on the sample with `count if namelast_ml!=namelast_ml_ditto` and compare summarize output for Jaro-Winkler scores computed from `namelast_ml` versus `namelast_ml_ditto`.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the description in line 141 to state that `namefrst_ml` is the raw model first name and `namelast_ml_ditto` is the ditto-resolved surname. If raw transcription benchmarking is intended, report Jaro-Winkler similarity on `namelast_ml` alongside or instead of `namelast_ml_ditto`.
findings.title: The generated report describes ditto-resolved surnames as raw model output
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 91-92 set `local l_ml namelast_ml_ditto`, using the ditto-resolved surname for similarity comparisons. Line 141 writes into the markdown report header: `Ours = raw model names (namefrst_ml, namelast_ml_ditto)`. While `namefrst_ml` is a raw model transcription, `namelast_ml_ditto` incorporates post-model ditto mark resolution, which is a separate inference step.
findings.why_it_matters: Describing ditto-resolved surnames as raw model names conflates transcription performance with downstream ditto resolution. Ditto marks (") are common in census records; resolving them is a separate inference step that alters both exact agreement and Jaro-Winkler similarity, so performance cannot be attributed solely to the OCR transcription model.

findings.how_to_check: Re-extract `refs_fullname.dta` from `profile_names.dta` into a temporary file and verify row-by-row identity. Check whether a stable record key like `unique_ID` or `histid` can be preserved in `refs_fullname.dta` and merged with `isid`.
findings.suggested_fix: Store a stable record identifier (`unique_ID` or `histid`) in `refs_fullname.dta` and merge on that key using `isid` and `assert(match)` rather than relying on arbitrary row index `_id = _n`.
findings.title: Split profile reference names are attached by positional row index rather than a stable key
findings.what_the_code_does: The script loads `profile_names.dta`, creates a positional row number with `gen long _id = _n`, and merges `refs_fullname.dta` on `_id` with `merge 1:1 _id using ... refs_fullname.dta, assert(match)`. It relies entirely on the assumption that `profile_names.dta` and `refs_fullname.dta` retain identical row ordering.
findings.why_it_matters: If `profile_names.dta` is reordered, updated, or re-extracted without synchronously rebuilding `refs_fullname.dta`, census records will be paired with the wrong profile names without triggering a merge assertion failure. Although lines 110-135 check aggregate exact agreement to one decimal place, minor row-order shifts could alter the three-decimal Jaro-Winkler means while passing the rounded exact agreement check.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to claims stated in the script comments and the generated markdown text.
Census microdata and intermediate datasets (profile_names.dta, refs_fullname.dta) reside outside the repository and could not be loaded; runtime behavior was inferred from Stata source reading.
The Stata execution pipeline was not run; runtime execution of the external SSC jarowinkler package could not be verified directly.
The output file MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md was not present in the repository, so emitted table values could not be inspected directly.
structured_output.summary: The Jaro-Winkler comparison script is defensively constructed: it guards against empty-string agreement inflation, ensures uniqueness for distinct-pair merges, and validates exact-agreement shares against benchmark numbers before generating output. The primary defect is in claims-vs-code: the generated report text describes the model names as 'raw' despite using the ditto-resolved surname namelast_ml_ditto, which incorporates a separate inference step. A secondary correctness vulnerability is merging cached reference names on a positional row index (_id = _n) rather than a stable record identifier.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
